one_sentence_story: Coined and tested via dual-ear headphone 'shadowing' by British engineer Colin Cherry in 1953, the Cocktail Party Problem showed that locking verbal attention onto one voice leaves you aware of an ignored voice's pitch or tone while rendering you completely deaf to its words — even if it switches into German.
so_what_for_you: Never pair two verbal streams at once (writing emails during a live meeting, or studying to lyric-heavy talk podcasts): because your brain can decode words from only one voice stream at a time, pause lyrics or chatter whenever deep verbal focus matters.
